info.title: WebMS Intra REST API
info.description: Internal portal platform REST API. Two mutually-exclusive auth modes are accepted on every endpoint: (1) an authenticated portal session (cookie-based) plus a valid CSRF token on write operations (passed via `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header or `csrf_token` body field), or (2) a site-scoped bearer API key (`Authorization: Bearer wbms_…`, minted at Admin → Integrations → API Keys). Bearer requests need NO CSRF token — CSRF protects cookie-based sessions from cross-site forgery and is meaningless for a bearer token that travels in an explicit Authorization header set by the calling code, never by a browser automatically. Bearer requests are tenant-pinned to the key's own site (regardless of the Host header) and are rate-limited per key (see `/api/v1/*` paths below). Every endpoint can be enabled/disabled per-site via the `api.{module}.{action}.enabled` setting; bearer requests resolve that flag against the KEY's site, not the host-detected default. An endpoint also follows its APP's own switch (Admin → Apps): when the app it belongs to is switched off for the organisation, every one of that app's endpoints, legacy and `/api/v1` alike, answers 403 with the message `The <app name> app is switched off for this organisation.`, before the per-endpoint setting is looked at. For a bearer request the app's switch is read for the KEY's site, whatever address the key is sent to. The `events` endpoints and the Event Team Hub endpoints belong to the Calendar app; the `users` endpoints belong to no app and are never refused this way. The `/api/v1/{resource}[/{id}]` paths are a thin RESTful facade: each verb maps onto the SAME handler file and the SAME `api.{app}.{action}.enabled` flag as its documented `/api/{app}/{action}` legacy alias — there are no separate permissions to manage. Events copied in from an outside calendar reach an API key exactly when a signed-out visitor could see them, in the same detail, unless the calendar — or a choice or rule covering the event — is set 'Don't show via API'.

sessionCookie.description: Portal session cookie set on sign-in.

csrfToken.name: X-CSRF-TOKEN
csrfToken.description: CSRF token. Read from `<meta name="csrf-token">` in the portal HTML or from the session. Required on POST endpoints; ignored on read-only GETs.

bearerAuth.description: Site-scoped API key from Admin → Integrations → API Keys; scopes gate each resource:verb; rate-limited per key; CSRF-exempt.

Error.description: A refusal. `meta` was missing from this schema until 27 October 2026 even though every refusal carries it: ApiResponse::error() builds its envelope from the same meta() as ApiResponse::success(). That matters to a caller making several writes without reloading, because meta.csrfToken is where the replacement form token arrives - on a refusal as well as on a success.

status.description: Always the text "error" on a refusal.

message.description: What went wrong, in words meant for a person. Safe to show to the caller.

detail.description: Extra detail for diagnosis. Present ONLY when the installation has debug mode switched on, which is for administrators; on an ordinary installation this field is absent altogether, so a caller must not depend on it.

meta.description: The same envelope block a successful answer carries. Includes csrfToken when a session-authenticated write has just replaced the form token.

status.description: Always the text "ok" on a successful answer. This example read "success" until 27 October 2026, which the portal has never sent: ApiResponse::success() writes 'status' => 'ok'.

timezone.description: The time zone the start and end are a clock reading in: a full IANA name. An event has exactly one; there is no second zone field.

status.description: The event's state. A draft is returned only to a caller who may manage events (an administrator session, or a key with events:write).

isPublic.description: 1 when a signed-out visitor could see this event. For your organisation's own events it is the event's own setting. For an event imported from an outside calendar it is worked out from who may see it, so it is always 1 in a reply to an API key.

location.description: Canonical cross-repo location object (#456) — additive; the legacy location* fields above are kept for backward compatibility.

imported.description: True when the event was copied in from an outside calendar (#514); false for the organisation's own events. The outside calendar itself, and every internal import or external setting, are never returned.

detailsLimited.description: True when this caller may see only the event's title, date and time (#514). Its description, every location field, the location object's contents, host and partner names, images and venue are then null. Only ever true for an imported event; the organisation's own events are always sent in full to a caller who may see them.

Location.description: Canonical location object shared byte-for-byte with the ProjectBookIT/ProjectEPass location contract (#456). Every field may be null; consumers must tolerate a partial object.

timezone.description: Optional. The time zone the start and end are a clock reading in: a full IANA name, spelled exactly. Left out, the event takes its organisation's own zone. A start or end given with an offset of its own is a moment, and is stored as this zone's clock reads at that moment. A name the portal does not know is refused with 422 and nothing is created.

locationGeoLat.description: Validated as a pair with locationGeoLng — either both present and valid, or the pair is stored as null (#456).

locationW3W.description: Bare canonical what3words form (no leading ///). A non-empty value that fails this pattern is rejected with a 422 (#456).

NoticeboardPoster.description: Poster as returned by GET /api/noticeboard/list (DB columns already mapped to the field names the board component reads).

id.description: Client-facing id; the literal string "p" + posterID.

kicker.description: Short eyebrow line shown above the title.

date.description: Set when schedule=once; empty string otherwise.

time.description: 24-hour HH:MM, or empty string if not set.

link.description: Official event page. The board opens this when the enlarged poster is tapped a second time.

mediaType.description: Text-only posters (no image/canva) are reported here as "image" with an empty image URL.

canva.description: Canva embed URL, for mediaType canva.

thumb.description: Optional board thumbnail override for Canva posters.

colorIndex.description: Index into the board's built-in accent-colour palette.

serif.description: true = editorial serif title font, false = bold sans-serif.

PosterInput.description: One poster in the `posters` array sent to POST /api/noticeboard/save. The client always sends the FULL desired board state — any existing poster whose id is missing from the array is soft-deleted.

id.description: Pass the existing "p<posterID>" to update that poster. Omit, or use a fresh client-generated id (e.g. "p<timestamp>"), to insert a new one — an id that doesn't belong to this site is treated as new rather than overwriting another site's poster.

title.description: Required — rows with an empty/whitespace-only title are silently skipped.

link.description: http(s):// absolute or a root-relative ("/…") path only — any other scheme (e.g. javascript:) is silently stripped to empty.

mediaType.description: Server-side derived value wins: forced to "canva" if canva is set, or "text" if neither canva nor image is set.

image.description: Media URL for image/video posters. data: URIs are rejected with 422 — upload via the media library and pass its URL instead.

canva.description: Canva embed/share URL. Must start with https://www.canva.com/ or it is discarded.

V1SuccessEnvelope.description: Standard success envelope returned by every /api/v1/* and legacy /api/{app}/{action} endpoint.

data.description: Endpoint-specific payload — see each operation's response schema.

csrfToken.description: Present ONLY on a write (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) that was authenticated by the caller's login session and passed its anti-forgery check. The portal issues a brand-new anti-forgery token every time it accepts one, so the token you just sent is now dead. Use this replacement on your next write, or you will be refused with "CSRF check failed". Requests authenticated with a bearer API key never receive this field, because they carry no session for a token to protect.

detail.description: Only present when the server is running in debug mode.

csrfToken.description: Present ONLY on a write (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) that was authenticated by the caller's login session and passed its anti-forgery check. The portal issues a brand-new anti-forgery token every time it accepts one, so the token you just sent is now dead. Use this replacement on your next write, or you will be refused with "CSRF check failed". Requests authenticated with a bearer API key never receive this field, because they carry no session for a token to protect.

serviceTypeID.description: FK tblAttendanceServiceTypes; must exist for the current site.

eventID.description: FK tblEvents; must exist for the current site.

AttendanceUpdate.description: PATCH-style — only fields present are touched. When `counts` is present, ALL existing headcount rows for the session are replaced (delete + re-insert).

DocumentCreate.description: Accepts EITHER multipart/form-data (file field `file`, session-UI parity) OR application/json with base64 `fileContent` (shown here — the bearer/device mode). The real MIME type is sniffed from the file bytes (finfo) and checked against a server-side allowlist — the client-declared type/extension is never trusted.

categoryID.description: FK tblDocCategories; must exist for the current site.

fileName.description: Original filename — cosmetic only; the stored filename + extension are server-generated from the sniffed MIME type.

fileContent.description: Base64-encoded file bytes. Capped by the `documents.api.maxUploadBytes` setting (default 10485760).

DocumentUpdate.description: Metadata only — v1 has no file-replacement endpoint (rotate via create + delete).

ExpenseCreate.description: `lineTotal` and the claim `totalAmount` are always computed server-side from `unitCost * quantity` — never accepted from the client. New claims always land in 'Pending' status; the approval/status-transition workflow is DEFERRED to Phase 3 (no `PUT /api/v1/expenses/{id}` exists in v1).

deptID.description: FK tblDepts; must exist for the current site and be active (#517). Departments and user groups, and their memberships, are managed at Admin -> Departments / Admin -> Groups and are not readable or writable through this API.

userID.description: REQUIRED for bearer (API-key) submissions only — the owning user, who must belong to the key's own site. Ignored/ not required in session mode, where the owner is always the authenticated session user.

UserCreate.description: Passwords are NEVER accepted here — the new account gets a random, unusable password hash and must go through the existing forgot-password flow to set a real one. `isAdmin` (portal-wide) is honoured in session mode only — a bearer key can never mint a portal admin, even with `users:write`; use `isSiteAdmin` (site-scoped) instead. #456 Chunk B: a member's Directory home coordinates/what3words (`latitude`/`longitude`/`what3words`/`visibilityCoords`, migration 181) are never readable or writable via this API in any mode — a deliberate safest-floor stance, since a bearer/session API caller has no per-viewer visibility-tier context to apply the member's own `visibilityCoords` gate against. #516: role holdings (`tblUserRoles`) are likewise never readable or writable through this API in any mode — grant or remove a role from the members page or Admin -> Roles instead. #517: group and department memberships (`tblUserGroups`, `tblUserDepts`) are likewise never readable or writable through this API in any mode.

isAdmin.description: Administrator rights across the whole portal (every organisation). Honoured only for a signed-in (session) request from a global administrator; a session request from anyone else that would change it is refused with 403. Ignored for API-key requests.

UserUpdate.description: Editable: fullName, isActive, isAdmin (session mode only), isSiteAdmin. Email address and password are excluded from v1 (silently ignored if present). A session caller can never deactivate their OWN account via this endpoint. Directory location fields are likewise excluded — see the `UserCreate` schema note (#456 Chunk B). Changing fullName or isActive on an account that belongs to a global administrator, has administrator rights across the whole portal, or also belongs (or used to belong) to another organisation is refused with 403 unless the caller is a global administrator using a signed-in session. Changing isSiteAdmin on a global administrator or a portal-wide administrator is refused the same way. An API key never counts as a global administrator.

isAdmin.description: Administrator rights across the whole portal (every organisation). Honoured only for a signed-in (session) request from a global administrator; from anyone else a request asking for it is refused with 403. Ignored for API-key requests.

Asset.description: A single asset row as returned by list/detail (#406). `licenseKey` and `publicToken` are ALWAYS stripped before this leaves the API (ApiResponse::filterSensitive()) — neither ever appears in a response, on any endpoint. `categoryName`/`locationName` are joined convenience fields.

purchaseCostPence.description: Integer minor units (pence) — house money convention #266.

currentValuePence.description: Last computed/valued book value, in pence.

isConfidential.description: When true the asset is hidden from non-privileged callers: list/detail/qr return it only to a logged-in session admin or asset_manager (detail/qr also to a responsible owner-party) — never to a bearer key or an ordinary logged-in user. Non-privileged callers get a uniform 404, not a 403.

AssetCreate.description: Unlike the HTML `save.php` form this mirrors, money fields here are PENCE INTEGERS (not pounds-decimal strings), and an invalid ENUM value (assetKind/conditionState/status/currency/depreciationMethod/labelSymbology) 400s rather than silently defaulting — see `_apps/assets/api/_coerce.php`. `licenseKey` travels as PLAINTEXT in the request body only — it is encrypted at rest and NEVER echoed back by any response. On update (PUT/PATCH), only fields present in the JSON body are touched; everything else keeps its current value.

categoryID.description: Site-scoped FK; silently dropped (NULL) if it doesn't resolve on this site.

locationID.description: Site-scoped FK; silently dropped (NULL) if it doesn't resolve on this site.

assetTagCode.description: UNIQUE per site — a collision returns 409.

purchaseCostPence.description: PENCE, not pounds — house money convention #266.

licenseKey.description: PLAINTEXT on write only. Blank/absent leaves it unchanged on update; blank means "no key" on create.

EventHubResource.description: One row from an event's Team Hub Resources list (GET /api/calendar/hub-resources) — a link or a free-text note, grouped into a free-text section label.

section.description: Free-text grouping label, e.g. "Before the event" / "On the day".

EventHubVideo.description: One row from an event's Team Hub video grid (GET /api/calendar/hub-videos). NEVER includes signing keys, playback tokens, or any cfstream.* credential — videoRef is the public provider ID/UID a player embeds against.

videoRef.description: YouTube 11-char ID / Vimeo numeric ID / Cloudflare Stream 32-hex UID — the public reference a player embeds against, never a secret.

requiresSignedUrl.description: cloudflare only — whether playback requires a signed URL. Policy metadata, not a token.

allowedOrigins.description: cloudflare only — comma-joined allowed embed origins.

messageID.description: The message's own number. Use the largest one you have seen as `sinceID` to fetch only what is new.

displayName.description: The name the sender gave, as tidied by the portal when the message was accepted.

body.description: The message itself, already shortened to the installation's maximum length when it was accepted.

createdAt.description: When the message was sent, as the database stores it. This is NOT formatted or converted to the reader's time zone by this endpoint.

WorshipDisplayState.description: Where a running service plan has got to. A flat object: this is NOT the portal's usual {status, data, meta} envelope.

currentItemID.description: The item being shown, or null when the plan has no saved position yet. **Blanking or blacking the screen does NOT null this** -- the item is kept so the operator can return to it, so `isBlank` and `isBlack` are the only reliable test for a blank screen. A client that treated null as "blank" would go on showing the slide the operator just blanked.

currentSlideIndex.description: Which slide of the current item is showing, counting from zero.

totalSlides.description: How many slides the current item has. Always 1 for anything that is not a song.

isBlank.description: True when the operator has blanked the screen, leaving the display's own background.

isBlack.description: True when the operator has blacked the screen out entirely.

slideTitle.description: The current slide's heading. Empty when there is no current item.

body.description: The current slide's text. Empty when there is no current item.

itemType.description: What kind of item is showing, for example a song or a reading. Empty when there is no current item.

allOf.description: The plan's new position, plus the replacement form token. Note the token is a TOP-LEVEL field here, not `meta.csrfToken`, because this handler does not use the portal's usual envelope. A console drawn once and used repeatedly must carry it into the next request.

csrfToken.description: The replacement form token. Send this with your next request; the one you just used is now dead.

Tour.description: A guided tour of part of the portal.

tourID.description: The tour's own number. Send it back to `POST /api/tours/complete` when the person finishes.

tourKey.description: A short name for the tour, for example `welcome`.

version.description: Which version of the portal this tour was written for.

title.description: The tour's name, as shown to the person.

steps.description: The tour's steps, in order, as stored when the tour was written. The portal checks only that this is a non-empty list.

HymnSearchResult.description: One hymn or song found by a search. The fields present depend on where it came from -- read `source` first.

source.description: `hymnal` is this organisation's own hymn book, `song` its song library, `remote` an outside catalogue.

songID.description: The song library's own number. Present for `song` results.

author.description: Who wrote it, where that is known.

ccliNumber.description: The song's CCLI number, used for usage reporting, where it is known.

hymnalCode.description: Which hymn book it is in.

hymnNumber.description: Its number in that hymn book. Present on `song` rows; a `hymnal` or `remote` row carries its own fields from the hymn book it came from, which this schema does not list.

FlatError.description: A refusal from one of the handlers that answers OUTSIDE the portal's usual {status, data, meta} envelope and sends no `ok` field with it. Test the HTTP status, not a field.

error.description: What went wrong. **Its style differs by endpoint, so do not show it blindly and do not match on it.** The livestream ping sends a short machine word (`method`, `json`, `token`, `event`); the push endpoints send a sentence meant for a person, such as "Please sign in to turn notifications on for this device." Decide behaviour from the HTTP status, not from this text.

get.summary: List an event's Team Hub resources (links + notes)
get.description: Requires scope `eventhub:read` (bearer) or an authenticated session. The event must belong to the caller's own site — a bearer key is tenant-pinned to the site it was minted for — or this 404s rather than revealing another tenant's event. A session is answered only for an event the calendar would show that person: a public event, or an internal one of an organisation they are an active member of or administer (#534); and only when that person is on the event's own team (an administrator, a coordinator of the event, a crew member, somebody with a job on it, or somebody named on the event as one of its people, such as a host or a speaker), which is the same test as the Team Hub page. Any other event is the same 404 as one that does not exist. A bearer key is not a person on a team: it is answered for the organisation's own events as before. Built for the projectBookIT Event Team Hub integration (#387).

The response NEVER includes a signing key, playback token, or any `cfstream.*` credential — only `videoRef` (the public provider ID/UID a player embeds against) and playback-policy metadata. post.summary: Replace the current site's poster set (site admins only)
post.description: Site admins only (App::isSiteAdmin()) — CSRF-protected via the X-CSRF-TOKEN header. The client sends the FULL desired poster array in one call; posters upsert by their "p<posterID>" id (a foreign or new-looking id inserts a fresh row instead of overwriting another tenant's poster), and any existing poster left out of the array is soft-deleted. The whole batch is validated before any row is written, and rolled back together on failure.

403.description: Admin access required, or endpoint disabled

422.description: Malformed payload — missing `posters` array, or a poster's image is a data: URI (upload via the media library instead)

500.description: Save failed — the whole batch was rolled back

get.description: Requires an authenticated session or an API key with scope `tasks:read`. A session returns tasks assigned to the caller; an administrator may choose another assignee with `userID`. Results are paginated, and `status` defaults to `open`. **Canonical route:** `GET /api/v1/tasks`.

get.summary: Messages approved for a livestream's chat
get.description:
Returns up to 100 approved messages for one event, oldest first. Only messages with status `approved` are ever returned, so anything waiting, hidden or flagged is invisible here.

**Who may read it.** The handler itself asks for no sign-in. What a caller may see is decided per event: a public event is readable by anybody, and an internal one only by a signed-in person who may see it AND whose request came from one of the portal's own pages. An event the caller may not see returns 200 with an empty list, exactly as a made-up event number does, so the answer never reveals that an event exists.

**Polling.** Pass the `lastID` you were last given as `sinceID` to fetch only what is new. The portal sets no interval and enforces none.

Refused with 403 while the `chat.enabled` setting is not `true`.

parameters.name: eventID
parameters.description: The event whose chat to read. Must be greater than zero.

parameters.name: sinceID
parameters.description: Return only messages with a higher `messageID` than this. Use the `lastID` from your previous call; 0 means from the beginning.

200.description: The messages, or an empty list for an event the caller may not see.

messages.description: Approved messages, oldest first, at most 100.

lastID.description: The `messageID` of the last message returned, or the `sinceID` you sent when there were none. Send it back as `sinceID` next time.

400.description: `eventID` was missing or not greater than zero.

403.description: Chat is switched off for this installation.

405.description: Only GET is accepted.

post.summary: Post a message to a livestream's chat
post.description:
Adds one message to an event's chat.

**No sign-in and no form token are asked for**, because the embedded player runs on other people's websites. Four other things stand in their place: chat must be switched on; the event must be one the caller may see; the `sessionToken` must already exist for this organisation and event, having been created by a livestream ping; and the FIRST message from a given token must pass the bot check when one is configured.

**Over-long text is shortened, not refused.** `body` is trimmed to the installation's maximum and only then refused if nothing is left.

**The message may not appear at once.** The reply's `status` says which happened: `approved` is live immediately, `pending` is waiting for a moderator, and `flagged` was caught by the profanity check -- which marks the message rather than refusing it.

A missing event, an event in another organisation and an event the caller may not see all answer 401 `Unknown session`, deliberately, so the reply is not an existence oracle.

sessionToken.description: The viewer's livestream session token, as created by `POST /api/livestream/ping`. It must already exist for this organisation and event.

displayName.description: The name to show beside the message. Tidied by the portal; a value that tidies to nothing is refused.

body.description: The message. Shortened to the installation's maximum length rather than refused, then refused only if nothing remains.

200.description: The message was stored. Read `status` to learn whether it is visible yet.

status.description: `approved` is visible now; `pending` awaits a moderator; `flagged` was caught by the profanity check and is held.

204.description: Answer to a cross-origin pre-flight (OPTIONS). No body.

400.description: `eventID`, `displayName` or `body` missing, `sessionToken` malformed, or the bot check failed.

401.description: The session token is unknown for this organisation and event, or the event is not one the caller may see. The two are deliberately indistinguishable.

403.description: Chat is switched off for this installation.

405.description: Only POST (and OPTIONS) are accepted.

429.description: Too many messages from this session token or this address. No `Retry-After` is sent.

503.description: The message could not be stored, or the bot check is configured but its keys cannot be read.

post.summary: Approve, hide or flag a chat message
post.description:
Sets one message's status. For a signed-in administrator, or somebody holding the `stream_moderator` role, in the organisation that owns the message.

**This answer carries a replacement form token in `meta.csrfToken`, and a page that moderates more than one message must keep it**: the portal replaces the token every time it accepts one, so a console drawn once and used repeatedly stops working after the first action without it. The replacement is also returned on every refusal raised after the token check.

A message in another organisation is reported as 404, the same as one that does not exist.

**Re-applying the status a message already has answers 200, not 404.** The refusal is decided by whether a row changed, and the same statement also stamps who moderated the message and when, so a repeat still changes the row. (The one exception is the same moderator repeating inside the same second, when nothing differs and the answer is 404.)

action.description: `approve` makes it visible, `hide` removes it from view, `flag` marks it for attention.

csrf_token.description: The form token. May be sent in the `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header instead, which wins when both are present.

200.description: The message's status is as asked. Also the answer when it already had that status, because the row still changes.

messageID.description: The message acted on, echoed back.

400.description: `action` was not one of the three, or `messageID` was not greater than zero.

401.description: Not signed in.

403.description: Not an administrator or `stream_moderator`, or the form token was wrong.

404.description: No such message in this organisation — or the same moderator repeating the same status inside the same second, when nothing in the row differs.

405.description: Only POST is accepted.

post.summary: Publish a prompt to an event's viewers
post.description:
Publishes one prompt to everybody watching an event. For a signed-in administrator, or the event's own coordinator.

**A session only — an API key cannot reach this.** Returns a replacement form token in `meta.csrfToken`; a console that publishes more than once must keep it.

**The form token is checked BEFORE the role is**, so a caller who is neither an administrator nor the coordinator, and whose token is also stale, is told the token was wrong rather than that they lack permission.

get.summary: What a service-plan display should be showing now
get.description:
The current position of a running service plan, for a projector screen or an operator's console to poll.

**This endpoint does NOT use the portal's usual `{status, data, meta}` envelope.** It answers its own flat object, and sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` so a display on another machine can read it. It carries none of the portal's usual security headers.

**It needs no sign-in.** The 64-character display token in `t` is the whole of the authority, and it is tied to one active plan in one organisation -- a token from another organisation answers 404.

**Polling:** the display polls about twice a second and the operator's console about once every one and a half seconds. Nothing is rate limited, so be careful what you point at it.

`totalSlides` is 1 for anything that is not a song.

post.summary: Move a running service plan on
post.description:
Moves a service plan to another item, or blanks the screen. For a signed-in administrator of the organisation, or the plan's event's coordinator.

**This endpoint does NOT use the portal's usual `{status, data, meta}` envelope**, and the replacement form token comes back as a **top-level `csrfToken`**, not as `meta.csrfToken`. A console that is drawn once and then used repeatedly MUST carry that value forward into its next request: without it every control works exactly once.

**What it changes is shared.** Every projector and console watching the same plan sees the move on its next poll of `/api/worship/state`. Moving into a song also records one line of song-usage reporting.

**Which refusals carry the replacement token:** it is absent from the 405, the 401, and the 400 raised by a failed token check, because all three are decided before a new token is issued. It is present on every other refusal -- the 400 for an unknown `action` or a bad `itemID`, the 403, and both 404s.

get.summary: The guided tour to offer this person next
get.description:
Returns the one tour the signed-in person should be shown next, or `null` when there is nothing to show. A tour already completed is never returned.

The welcome tour comes first when it is switched on, then the newest other tour. A tour limited to particular roles is offered to somebody holding one of them **or to any administrator**, who is never filtered out by the role test.

**It answers 200 with `data: null` rather than an error when it cannot read the tours at all**, so a portal with the tours table missing simply offers no tour. The only refusal is 401.

data.description: The tour to offer, or `null` when there is nothing to show.

401.description: Not signed in.

post.summary: Record that this person finished a tour
post.description:
Marks one tour as completed for the signed-in person, so it is not offered again. Always for the caller's own account: a tour cannot be completed on somebody else's behalf.

**Safe to call twice** -- a repeat leaves the original completion time alone.

Returns a replacement form token in `meta.csrfToken`, which a page that calls this more than once must keep. The 401, 405 and 403 below are decided before the token is issued, so they do not carry it.

**The sign-in check runs before the method check**, so a GET from a caller who is not signed in answers 401 rather than 405.

post.summary: Tell the portal a viewer is still watching
post.description:
Opens or refreshes a viewer's watching session, and closes it when they leave. This is what creates the `sessionToken` that `POST /api/livechat/send` needs.

**This endpoint does NOT use the portal's usual `{status, data, meta}` envelope**; it answers a flat `{"ok":true}`. It sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on purpose, because the embedded player runs on other people's websites, and it carries none of the portal's usual security headers.

**No sign-in and no form token are asked for.** A ping naming no event is accepted from anybody. A ping naming an event must name one the caller may see -- for an internal event that means a signed-in person whose request came from one of the portal's own pages. An internal, draft, other-organisation or made-up event all answer 404 alike, so the reply does not say which.

**A `leaving` ping skips the event check entirely**, because it only closes the caller's own session row. Note it matches on the token alone and is not scoped to an organisation.

sessionToken.description: The viewer's own token: 32 to 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, which the caller generates and then reuses for every ping and chat message.

token.description: The older embed snippet's name for `sessionToken`. `sessionToken` wins when both are sent.

eventID.description: The event being watched. Omit, or send 0, for a ping that names no event.

leaving.description: Send exactly `true` (not `"true"`, not 1) to close this watching session. Anything else counts as false.

200.description: The ping was recorded. A flat object, not the usual envelope.

204.description: Answer to a cross-origin pre-flight (OPTIONS). No body.

400.description: A flat refusal of this handler's own making.

404.description: A flat refusal of this handler's own making.

405.description: A flat refusal of this handler's own making.

get.summary: What is booked, day by day, across a date range
get.description:
Returns the bookings for one venue, or for every venue, across a range of dates. For any signed-in person who may view venues; an API key cannot reach this.

**These are calendar dates, not moments.** `from` and `to` are read as plain dates and no time zone is applied to them.

**No cost information is ever returned** by this endpoint.

**One refusal covers four different causes.** A caller who may not view venues, a malformed or backwards date range, a range longer than 400 days, and a venue that does not belong to this organisation ALL answer 400 with the same `invalid-range` message -- deliberately, so the reply cannot be used to discover which venues exist.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First date to report on, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last date to report on, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Must not be before `from`, and the range must be 400 days or fewer.

parameters.name: venueID
parameters.description: Limit to one venue. Omit, or send 0, for every venue this organisation has.

days.description: One entry per date in the range, keyed by the date as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

items.description: One booking. Cost columns are never included.

400.description: Not permitted to view venues, a malformed or backwards range, a range over 400 days, or a venue that is not this organisation's. All four say `invalid-range`.

401.description: Not signed in.

get.summary: Whether a venue and room are free for a proposed time
get.description:
Classifies a proposed start and end against what is already booked, for the event editor to warn on a clash before anything is saved. For any signed-in person; an API key cannot reach this.

**`start` and `end` are readings on a clock, not moments in history**, and are used together with `tz`. **`tz` defaults to `Europe/London` and is NOT the organisation's own time zone** -- send it explicitly for any organisation that is not in the United Kingdom, or the answer will be an hour or more out.

**This endpoint does not refuse much.** A caller without permission to view venues, and an unknown venue, both answer 200 reporting that there is no venue to check, so it cannot be used to discover which venues exist. An unknown **room** is different: it falls back to classifying the venue as a whole rather than reporting nothing. It also does NOT check that `end` is after `start`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The proposed start, as a reading on a clock: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: The proposed end, in the same form. May be left empty, which means no end is being proposed. Not checked against `start`.

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description: The time zone `start` and `end` are readings in, as a zone name such as `Europe/London` or `America/New_York`. **Defaults to `Europe/London`, not to the organisation's own zone.**

parameters.name: venueID
parameters.description: The venue to check. When omitted the `venues.calendar_default_venue` setting is used, which an organisation may set for itself.

parameters.name: roomID
parameters.description: A room within the venue. Omit to check the venue as a whole.

200.description: How the proposed time compares with what is booked. Also the answer when the caller may not view venues, or the venue or room is unknown.

data.description: The classification of the proposed time against existing bookings.

400.description: `start` missing or malformed, `end` present but malformed, or `tz` is not a zone name the server knows. All say `invalid-range`.

401.description: Not signed in.

post.summary: Create a member account
post.description:
The legacy address of `POST /api/v1/users`, reaching the same handler. **This address does work** -- the handler's own method gate names POST, and that gate is only relaxed, never tightened, when the request arrives through the v1 facade.

**A signed-in caller must be an administrator.** A bearer key is gated by the `users:write` scope alone -- nothing in the key path performs an administrator test -- plus the `api.users.create.enabled` switch, **which ships switched off**.

**No password is set.** The new account gets an unusable one, so the person must use the existing forgot-password flow to choose their own.

**`isAdmin` is only honoured for a signed-in global administrator** and is silently ignored for a bearer key.

isActive.description: 1 when the account may sign in.

isAdmin.description: 1 when the account administers the whole portal.

isSiteAdmin.description: 1 when the account administers this organisation.

siteID.description: The organisation the account was given membership of.

401.description: Not signed in, or the bearer key is invalid or expired.

403.description: Not an administrator, the bearer key lacks `users:write`, the form token was wrong, or `isAdmin` was asked for by somebody who is not a global administrator.

409.description: That e-mail address is already in use, or is in use somewhere the caller cannot see.

429.description: Too many address checks from this administrator or key. A `Retry-After` header says how long to wait.

500.description: The account could not be created; nothing was written.

post.summary: Change a member account
post.description:
The legacy address of `PUT`/`PATCH /api/v1/users/{id}`, reaching the same handler. **This address does work**, with the account number in `?id=` or as `userID` in the body.

**A signed-in caller must be an administrator.** A bearer key is gated by the `users:write` scope alone -- nothing in the key path performs an administrator test -- plus the `api.users.update.enabled` switch, **which ships switched off**.

At least one of `fullName`, `isActive`, `isAdmin` or `isSiteAdmin` must be sent. **`isAdmin` is read only for a signed-in caller** and ignored for a bearer key -- so a key sending only `isAdmin` is refused for having sent nothing to change.

**A request that changes nothing writes nothing** and answers 200 with the stored values, on purpose, so re-sending a value cannot overwrite somebody else's concurrent change. Note the limit this leaves: a field that IS changing is read and then written two statements apart, without locking the row.

**`emailAddress` and any password field are silently ignored.** You cannot deactivate your own account through this endpoint.

parameters.description: The account to change. May be sent as `userID` in the body instead.

isAdmin.description: 1 when the account administers the whole portal.

isSiteAdmin.description: 1 when the account administers this organisation.

post.summary: Register this device for push notifications
post.description:
Stores a browser's push details so the portal can notify this device.

**A signed-in person is required** -- this was not always so, and a request that is not signed in is now refused with 401 before anything else is read. A form token is required too.

**This endpoint does NOT use the portal's usual `{status, data, meta}` envelope.** It answers a flat object, and the replacement form token arrives as a top-level `csrf_token`, not as `meta.csrfToken`. Its answers carry none of the portal's usual security headers.

**Re-registering a device re-points it at whoever is signed in now**, because the stored row is keyed on the endpoint. A channel the portal does not recognise is dropped in silence rather than refused; if that leaves nothing, the default pair is used.

**Rate limited to 30 requests an hour per address, shared with `POST /api/push/unsubscribe`** -- the two endpoints count against one allowance. No `Retry-After` is sent.

auth.description: The device's authentication secret, base64url, decoding to exactly 16 bytes.

channels.description: Which kinds of notification this device wants. Anything the portal does not recognise is dropped silently. Defaults to `livestream` and `reminders`.

csrf_token.description: The form token. May be sent in the `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header instead.

channels.description: The channels actually stored, after any the portal does not recognise were dropped.

csrf_token.description: The replacement form token. Use it on your next request; the one you just sent is dead.

405.description: Only POST is accepted.

post.summary: Stop push notifications to this device
post.description:
Switches one device's push registration off. The row is kept and marked inactive rather than deleted.

**No sign-in is required**, deliberately: knowing the device's own push address is treated as proof enough, so a device whose person has gone can still switch itself off. A form token is still required.

**This endpoint does NOT use the portal's usual envelope**; the replacement form token arrives as a top-level `csrf_token`.

**It answers `ok: true` even when the address matched nothing**, and it is not scoped to an organisation -- a known address is switched off whichever organisation the request arrived at. Unlike subscribing, the address is not checked against the push services the portal recognises.

**Rate limited to 30 requests an hour per address, shared with `POST /api/push/subscribe`.** No `Retry-After` is sent.

csrf_token.description: The form token. May be sent in the `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header instead; note an EMPTY header is used as given and the body is not then consulted.

405.description: Only POST is accepted.

post.summary: Record a scanned asset during a stocktake
post.description:
Records one scan against an open stocktake run -- the same action the stocktake screen performs, so a hand-held scanner can use it directly.

Needs the `assets:write` scope for a bearer key, or a signed-in administrator with a form token.

**A confidential asset is reported back without its name or number to a bearer key** -- `assetName` becomes `(confidential asset)` and `assetID` is left out altogether. `verifyStatus` is always returned and the scan is always recorded, so hiding the identity never hides that a scan happened.

**Every failure answers 404**: an unknown run, a run already closed and a code that is not recognised are deliberately indistinguishable. The message says which in words, but the status does not.

**For a bearer key the scan is recorded against no person**, because a key is not somebody.

stocktakeID.description: The open stocktake run to record against.

code.description: The code that was scanned, as read from the label.

foundLocationID.description: Where the asset was actually found. A value that does not resolve is dropped rather than refused.

csrf_token.description: The form token, for a signed-in caller. May be sent in the `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header instead. Not used by a bearer key.

verifyStatus.description: What the scan established about the asset, for example that it was found where it was expected. Always present.

assetID.description: The asset that was scanned. **Left out entirely** when a bearer key scans a confidential asset.

assetName.description: The asset's name, or the fixed text `(confidential asset)` when a bearer key scans a confidential asset.

400.description: `stocktakeID` was not greater than zero, or `code` was empty.

401.description: Not signed in, or the bearer key is invalid or expired.

403.description: Not an administrator, the bearer key lacks `assets:write`, or the form token was wrong.

404.description: No such stocktake run, the run is already closed, or the code is not recognised. The three are deliberately indistinguishable by status.

405.description: Only POST is accepted.

429.description: The bearer key's rate limit. A `Retry-After` header says how long to wait.

post.summary: Upload a picture or video for a noticeboard poster
post.description:
Takes one picture or video and stores it outside the web root, returning the address to show it at.

**Send it as `multipart/form-data`, and put the form token in the `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header** -- it CANNOT go in the body here, because the body is the file rather than JSON.

**The file's type is decided by inspecting its contents**, never from its name or the type the caller declares. Only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, MP4 and WebM are accepted. The stored name is generated by the portal and the caller's filename is never used.

**The returned address is built for this organisation** and the picture is then served by a public address that needs no sign-in, because posters are shared by QR code.

The size limit is the installation's `noticeboard.upload.maxBytes`, falling back to 15 MB if that is not usable, so the cap can never be switched off. Note the web server's own upload limits apply first and produce a 400 of their own.

A signed-in caller must be an administrator of this organisation. A bearer key needs the `noticeboard:write` scope, and the organisation-administrator test does not apply to it: a key's authority is its scope.

file.description: The picture or video. Its real type is sniffed from the contents; the filename and declared type are ignored.

url.description: Where to show the file. Built for this organisation, and served by an address that needs no sign-in.

mediaType.description: Which of the two kinds it turned out to be, from the sniffed type.

400.description: No file was sent, the upload failed or was cut short, the file was empty, it was over the size limit, or its sniffed type is not one of the six allowed. The message says which.

401.description: Not signed in, or the bearer key is invalid or expired.

403.description: Not an administrator of this organisation, the bearer key lacks `noticeboard:write`, or the form token was wrong or was not sent in the `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header.

405.description: Only POST is accepted.

429.description: The bearer key's rate limit. A `Retry-After` header says how long to wait.

500.description: The file could not be read, inspected, saved, or recorded. When recording fails the saved file is removed again.

get.summary: Search hymns and songs while building a service plan
get.description:
Searches this organisation's hymn book and song library, and an outside catalogue when one is configured, for the service-plan editor's type-ahead. Any signed-in person; an API key cannot reach this.

**Read `source` on each result to know where it came from** -- the three groups are returned one after another in a single list, local hymn book first.

**Nothing here is refused for being too long or too large.** `q` is shortened to 100 characters and `limit` is forced into the range 1 to 25, both silently. An empty `q` returns an empty list at once.

**It degrades quietly rather than failing.** A problem reading the song library leaves that group simply missing from an otherwise normal 200, and an outside catalogue that cannot be reached is skipped while `remoteAttempted` still reports true. So `remoteAttempted` tells you the outside search was switched on, NOT that it succeeded.

The organisation is always taken from the session; it can never be chosen by the caller.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What to search for. Shortened to 100 characters rather than refused. Empty returns an empty list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many results to return per group. Forced into the range 1 to 25 rather than refused.

200.description: The results, or an empty list.

results.description: The matches, local hymn book first, then the song library, then the outside catalogue.

remoteAttempted.description: True when searching the outside catalogue is switched on. It does NOT mean that search succeeded -- a failure is skipped in silence.

401.description: Not signed in.
